projects.name: DeepSeek Harness
projects.oneLiner: A production-grade agent harness built on the Cordis plugin framework: everything is a plugin, configuration is composition, and events are extension points.

concepts.title: Profile and bundle layering
concepts.body: A profile lists the bundles to stack, and a bundle is the distribution format for Cordis config lines; at boot they apply to an empty entry list in the order "bundle sequence → profile patch → home patch → --patch", and any line can be overridden by a higher layer. Every line of the tree printed by dsh --profile web --dump-config is patchable.

concepts.title: Visible to the model means logged
concepts.body: Everything that enters a model request must be reconstructible from the session log — a runtime invariant asserts it. The only correct way to add a new model-visible input is to add a SessionEvent type and render it from the log.

concepts.title: Capability seams
concepts.body: A seam is formed by a service definition, its provider, and its consumers in triad; the filesystem and subprocess providers share one execution world — point both at a remote sandbox and Bash, PTY, and LSP migrate wholesale, with no consumer changes.

concepts.title: turn / step event flow
concepts.body: A step is one model request plus its tool calls; a turn is zero or more steps. agent/pre-step decides what the model sees (rewrite or reject); the three tools/* events form a waterfall where next() must be called; agent/turn-stopping is a serial interception point with no next().

projects.name: OpenClaw
projects.oneLiner: A personal AI assistant runtime with the Gateway at its core: 138 extensions, 57 skills — messaging channels as plugins.

concepts.title: The Gateway hub
concepts.body: A long-running gateway process unifies access to Discord, Telegram, and other channels; sessions, scheduling, and plugin orchestration all converge on the gateway side. packages/ defines the protocol/reasoning boundary with gateway-protocol, agent-core, and llm-runtime.

concepts.title: Extensions as capabilities
concepts.body: extensions/ holds 138 directories: model providers (anthropic, deepseek), channels (discord), tools (browser, canvas), diagnostics (diagnostics-otel), admin plane (admin-http-rpc) — load registers, unload rolls back.

concepts.title: Skill progressive disclosure
concepts.body: skills/ declares trigger conditions and instructions in SKILL.md, loading the body on demand: the most complete productized sample of the book's Chapter-2 "progressive disclosure" principle.

concepts.title: Snapshot and shallow sync
concepts.body: This repo keeps up via shallow fetch (git fetch --depth=1 origin main && git reset --hard origin/main); an unpacked snapshot under Reference/ makes the source easy to read straight through.

projects.name: Hermes Agent
projects.oneLiner: A complete single-machine self-evolving agent: gateway, agent, and 61 state-machine modules — the host of Chapter 9's self-modification experiment.

concepts.title: The state layer is the heart
concepts.body: The 61 hermes_state_*.py files at the repo root split session state into fine-grained modules — WAL, locks, lineage, compaction, rewind. Engineering "state consistency" as a first-class citizen: the densest real-world state-management sample in the book.

concepts.title: gateway + agent layering
concepts.body: gateway manages process and session lifecycles, agent/ runs the reasoning loop, toolsets.py and tools/ assemble tools; each layer can be swapped and experimented with independently.

concepts.title: Evals built in
concepts.body: evals/ and trajectory_compressor.py are the runnable counterparts of the book's "verifier" and "trajectory compression" chapters — verification is not a bolted-on test suite but the agent's own organ.

concepts.title: Self-evolution host
concepts.body: Chapter 9's propose–verify–canvass–rollback workflow drills on this repo as host (chapter9/hermes-self-evolution and downstream ablation tests coexist in-repo).

projects.name: PyCore
projects.oneLiner: A modular async-first Python backend skeleton: plugin registry, state-machine service layer, FastAPI integration — the common foundation of the book's experiment code.

concepts.title: Six-layer stack
concepts.body: core (config/logging/errors/Result schema) → plugins (registry-based plugin system) → services (state-machine service layer) → execution (flow execution and context) → api (FastAPI integration) → integrations (LLM and other external services).

concepts.title: Minimally readable
concepts.body: One file per concept, about a hundred lines per file — read the mechanisms here first, then step up to production repos; the gentlest learning slope.

concepts.title: Experiment foundation
concepts.body: The runtime skeleton of the book's experiment code is isomorphic to the services/flow abstractions here: services carry state machines, flows carry orchestration.
